record.context_brief: when convex realizability forces geometric k-orbit symmetry
record.original_question: For which pairs (k, d) is the following true: if a combinatorially k-orbit d-polytope P is realizable as a convex d-polytope, then P must actually be isomorphic to a geometrically k-orbit convex polytope?

evidence.quote: Problem 28. For what values of k and d is it true that, if a k-orbit d-polytope P is realized as a convex d-polytope, then P must be isomorphic to a geometrically k-orbit convex polytope?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract d-polytope is a partially ordered set P (with a least and greatest element) satisfying the standard axioms of abstract polytopes: it is ranked with ranks -1,0,1,...,d, every flag (maximal chain) has exactly d+2 elements, P is strongly flag-connected, and it satisfies the diamond condition (for any two elements F<G with rank(G)-rank(F)=2 there are exactly two elements strictly between them). The automorphism group Γ(P) acts on the set of flags of P; the polytope P is called combinatorially k-orbit if Γ(P) has exactly k orbits on flags.

A convex d-polytope Q in Euclidean space is the convex hull of finitely many points whose affine hull has dimension d; its face lattice (with the empty face and Q adjoined) is an abstract d-polytope. The Euclidean symmetry group G(Q) of Q consists of all isometries of the ambient space that map Q to itself; G(Q) acts on the flags of (the face lattice of) Q. The convex polytope Q is called geometrically k-orbit if G(Q) has exactly k orbits on the flags of Q.

We say an abstract d-polytope P is realized as a convex d-polytope if there is a convex d-polytope Q whose face lattice is isomorphic to P as an abstract polytope.

Problem. Determine all pairs (k,d) of positive integers with the following property: whenever a combinatorially k-orbit abstract d-polytope P admits a realization as a convex d-polytope, there exists a convex d-polytope Q whose face lattice is isomorphic to P and such that Q is geometrically k-orbit.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as one of 35 open problems on k-orbit abstract polytopes and we found no published resolution. Subsequent work has addressed related questions on automorphism groups and symmetry type graphs of k-orbit polytopes but does not resolve this convex-realizability vs. geometric-symmetry question.
